sn12.38:1.2: “Intend” (_ceteti_) and “plan” (_pakappeti_) play the role of “choices” (_saṅkhāra_), while “underlying tendencies” (_anuseti_) stand for “ignorance”.
sn12.38:1.3: That is, it takes rebirth in a new life.
sn12.38:1.4: It “grows” as the individual grows up and matures, leading to renewal of the cycle (see [mn38:28.1]()).
sn12.38:2.1: Normally, underlying tendencies manifest as moral choices. Here the Buddha suggests this is not always the case. But so long as the tendencies are still there, one is not freed.
sn12.38:3.5: This Sutta illustrates the threefold pattern (_tivaṭṭa_) into which dependent origination was later analyzed. The twelve factors may all be grouped under three headings: ignorance, craving, and grasping are “defilements” (_kilesavaṭṭa_); choices and continued existence are “deeds” (_kammavaṭṭa); the remainder are “results” (_vipākavaṭṭa_). Within these groups we may find different synonyms or related terms used in particular purposes. The least fitting in this scheme is _bhava_, which includes all three, but is counted under “deeds” here as it connects grasping with rebirth.
